\[
I_{\text{out}}(x,y) = \sum_{j=-r}^{r} \sum_{i=-r}^{r} M(i,j)\, I(x+i,\, y+j),
\qquad
M(i,j) = \frac{\ell(i,j)}{L},
\qquad
L = 9,
\quad
\theta = 0^{\circ}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input channel value
- \(I_{\text{out}}\): Output channel value
- \(M(i, j)\): Kernel weight at offset i to the right and j down
- \(\ell(i, j)\): Length of the line segment inside the unit square of cell (i, j)
- \(L\): Length of the motion in pixels
- \(\theta\): Angle of the motion, counterclockwise from the x axis
- \(r\): Kernel radius in pixels, the smallest one that holds the whole segment

The kernel is a line segment of length L through the center of the window, at angle theta. The weight of each cell is the length of the segment that passes through that cell's square, divided by L. The weights add up to 1. A slanted line gets smooth, anti-aliased weights instead of a jagged staircase.
